contract: Numbered invoices of one currency in plain Ecto/Postgrex tables on PostgreSQL 19 under the state/tenant-isolation floor (five tables: invoices UNIQUE (tenant, series, number), lines, applications, reversals keyed by reversal_id, series with the last number). An invoice is drafted for one billing account, currency and series (create/3 idempotent by invoice_id), takes up to 256 lines idempotent by line_id: a :usage line of the total of a complete domain/pricing charge (incomplete_charge otherwise; source_ref card_id/version/period), a :fee line of a domain/plan fee line taken as data (source_ref subscription_id/index) and :adjustment lines, all in the invoice's currency (currency otherwise), never negative on an invoice. finalize/3 locks the invoice row (for a credit note first the corrected invoice's), then the series row (created on first use with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING), takes the series' next number from 1 and freezes the lines in the same transaction, so committed finalizations of one series have consecutive numbers, a rolled-back one uses none and a void keeps its number; an invoice becomes :open, or :paid when its payable is zero; a non-zero total names the domain/journal operation invoice/<invoice_id>/issue as a pending posting, a zero total none; a repeat returns the same number and operation ID with duplicate true. mark_posted/3 records the host's journal result. apply_payment/3 applies a positive amount to an :open invoice up to its payable (total minus issued credit notes), idempotent by payment_ref, and makes it :paid at the payable. reverse_payment/3 takes back an amount, or :remaining fixed in its row, of one application up to what of it is still applied (over_reversal, nothing_applied, unknown_payment), idempotent by its own reversal_id, and reopens a :paid invoice whose paid drops below the payable. void/3 voids a :draft or :open document with nothing paid and nothing credited at the expected revision. credit_note/3 drafts a credit note of 1..256 negative adjustment lines of an :open or :paid invoice within its payable, checked again at its finalize/3 under the corrected invoice's row lock; issued, it grows the corrected invoice's credited and may make it :paid; get/3 shows an excess of paid over the payable as credit_balance. Every write checks shape (invalid), then the caller's transaction (in_transaction) before any query, runs in its own transaction at a checked READ COMMITTED Need (isolation) and locks the invoice row first; amounts are stored as Elzoo.Money.Codec bytes and summed with domain/money only. Fixed error atoms that echo no ID or amount; a database failure is unavailable. No journal post, tax, discount, rendering or multi-currency invoice.
limits: The Piece posts nothing: the host posts each finalized non-zero total to domain/journal under the named operation ID, chooses the accounts, the billing account and the series, and reads payment and refund outcomes from domain/payment-lifecycle; this Piece records what it is given and moves no money (a credit_balance is the host's to refund or carry).
A gapless number means no gap among committed finalizations of one series of one tenant; a draft or a void never releases a number, and a voided invoice keeps its number.
No tax, discount, rendering, delivery to a customer or multi-currency invoice; an incomplete charge is refused, never taken with a marker.

The state/tenant-isolation limits apply: the table owner can turn forcing off or drop the policies, and a superuser or BYPASSRLS role ignores them, so production connects as a non-owner, non-bypass application role with the README grants. The consumer Repo's query telemetry still receives the scope parameters (the tenant).
READ COMMITTED is a consumer Need that the Piece checks (current_setting('transaction_isolation') before any table query) but cannot set.

domain/pricing is a test-only dependency (the tests build charges with Elzoo.Pricing.price/3); the library code reads a charge as data and calls no domain/pricing, domain/plan or domain/journal function.
A database failure, including a lost connection, is {:error, :unavailable} and says nothing about whether the write committed; the outcome is left to a retry with the same request.

Concurrency (numbering, credit-note finalization, payments and reversals behind a held row lock), lock order and row-security evidence are finite scenarios on one local PostgreSQL 19 with repeated runs, not proofs; there are no Cure laws.

grounding.claim: Listed scenarios on the worker's own disposable PostgreSQL 19 database with DBConnection.ConnectionPool Repos (not the Sandbox) connected as the ELZ-285 application role with only the README grants (fails when ELZOO_TEST_APP_ROLE is unset), in random schemas dropped afterwards; after every case the stored state agrees with itself (each total the sum of its lines, each paid the applications minus their reversals with no application reversed past its amount, each credited the magnitude sum of its issued credit notes, the numbers of each series exactly 1..last_number, an open or paid invoice paid exactly when paid >= payable, a posting exactly for a finalized non-zero total). 1 two finalizations of two invoices of one series held behind another connection's series row lock until both wait in pg_locks get 1 and 2; a finalization whose transaction a test-only Repo wrapper fails after it took number 1 is unavailable, commits nothing and the next finalization takes 1; series independent; a void keeps its number; 2 an incomplete charge incomplete_charge, a complete charge one :usage line of its total with source_ref card_id/version/period, a plan fee line one :fee line with source_ref subscription_id/index, a zero fee line accepted, another currency's adjustment, charge and fee currency, line duplicate and conflict, a line after finalize {:state, :open}; 3 a repeated finalize the same number and operation ID with duplicate true, a finalize with no line or due before issue invalid, mark_posted applied, duplicate, another operation ID conflict; 4 two payments of 60 on a 100 invoice held behind another connection's invoice row lock until both wait in pg_locks give one applied and one over_payment with paid 60, a partial payment open, the rest paid, an over-payment over_payment, a repeated payment_ref duplicate, another amount conflict, a paid or draft invoice {:state, _}; 5 two reversals of 60 of a 100 payment behind the invoice row lock give one applied and one over_reversal with paid 40, a reversal_id equal to a payment_ref, a partial reversal of 30 of 100 reopens the paid invoice, its repeat reversed once, a :remaining reversal takes back 70 and its repeat duplicate, a third nothing_applied, a reversal over what is still applied over_reversal, unknown_payment; 6 void of a draft and of an open invoice (number kept, its pending posting kept and then recorded posted by mark_posted/3), stale_revision, paid_amount, credited, an issued credit note {:state, :issued}, a draft credit note voided, a draft credit note of an invoice voided meanwhile {:state, :void} at finalize, over_credit at credit_note/3 and at the second finalize of two drafts that together pass the payable, sequential and behind the corrected invoice's row lock (one finalized, one over_credit), an issued -40 credit note numbered from the same series with a pending posting, a 61 payment over_payment and a 60 payment paid, a repeated credit_note/3 paused (by a Repo telemetry handler) after its read of the not yet created credit note while the first call creates and finalizes it, then duplicate although the payable is now below its magnitude, a credit balance of 40 on a paid 100 invoice, a credit note that reaches paid = payable makes the invoice paid, a zero-total invoice paid with no posting, a credit note with a non-negative total invalid_total; 7 verify/1 ok, another tenant's invoice unknown_invoice from get, apply_payment, finalize and credit_note, no T2 row visible under T1, a direct T2 insert and DELETE on each table 42501, a caller transaction in_transaction from every function with no query on the Repo, a repeatable read Repo isolation from every write with nothing committed, a missing schema unavailable from every function; bounds of every text, the 256-line and 1..256 credit-note line bounds, new/1 refusals and the migration prefix ArgumentError. Negative controls by temporary edit: reading the last number before locking the series row fails case 1 (both read 0; the second insert of number 1 is refused by the unique index and is unavailable), allowing a line of another currency fails case 2, reversing the whole application instead of the amount fails case 5, and dropping FOR UPDATE from the corrected invoice's lock in finalize/3, from apply_payment/3's or from reverse_payment/3's invoice row lock fails the matching concurrent case of 6, 4 or 5, and skipping the check for a credit note created while credit_note/3 waited for the corrected invoice's lock makes the paused repeat over_credit. Finite scenarios, not proofs.

PostgreSQL 19 row locks (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE and FOR SHARE), READ COMMITTED re-reads after a lock wait, INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING waiting on a concurrent uncommitted insert, unique indexes with distinct NULLs, transaction rollback and row-level security are upstream server contracts reached through Postgrex 0.22.4.
Ecto SQL 3.14.0 Repo.transact/2 results and rollback, in_transaction?/0 and Ecto.Migration.execute/1 are upstream behavior, reached through Elzoo.TenantIsolation.transact/3.
Elixir String.valid?/1, the utf8 binary pattern and integer arithmetic for the text rule and the number of a series.
OTP 29.1.2 :crypto.hash(:sha256, iodata) computes the request digest of create/3 and credit_note/3.

The consumer runs the migration as the table owner, connects the application as a non-owner, non-bypass role with only the README grants at READ COMMITTED, calls Elzoo.Invoice.verify/1 at startup, keeps code that holds the connection from calling set_config itself, posts each finalized non-zero total under its operation ID and records the result with mark_posted/3, and retries an unavailable result with the same request.

telemetry.contract: The Piece emits no event and no log; its queries pass log: false. The consumer Repo's query telemetry still receives the scope parameters, the tenant-isolation limit.

config.contract: The binding from new/1 (exactly repo: and prefix: under the identifier rule, else {:error, :invalid}), fixed per binding; fixed Contract bounds: 1..256 lines per document, 1..100-byte invoice_id, 1..128-byte billing_account, series, line_id and tenant, 1..256-byte source_ref, payment_ref and reversal_id, 1..1,024-byte description, times 0..2^63-1, amounts within the domain/money range. No ambient or hot configuration.

control.contract: No process or lifecycle; void/3 and reverse_payment/3 are data operations, and the consumer owns the Repo, the migrations and the database roles.
